metadata.title: Advanced Linux
metadata.description: The deep end. Compose professional pipelines, script with conditionals, then crack the Operator tier where the flag belongs to root and only the right technique sets it free.

chapters.title: Advanced: composition and evidence
chapters.description: Compose tools like a professional: feed files in as input, keep copies of evidence while you work, and spot what changed between versions.
chapters.summary: Compose tools like a professional: feed files in as input, keep copies of evidence while you work, and spot what changed between versions.
skills: Save output while viewing it with tee

exercises.title: Read through standard input
exercises.description: Decode the receipt using base64 with input redirection.

exercises.title: Keep a copy of the evidence
exercises.description: Filter the OK line from source.log and save exactly that line to evidence.txt.

exercises.title: Spot a changed line
exercises.description: Compare before.txt and after.txt and recover the newly added flag.

exercises.title: Undo a reversed transmission
exercises.description: Reverse the characters of reversed.txt to recover the flag.

chapters.title: Advanced: variables and recovery
chapters.description: Make the shell remember things and recover from problems. Variables, directory permissions and conditional commands appear in every real script.
chapters.summary: Make the shell remember things and recover from problems. Variables, directory permissions and conditional commands appear in every real script.
skills: Set and use variables with export and $NAME

exercises.title: Store the route
exercises.description: Set DEST to /opt/academy/signal, then use "$DEST/receipt" to read the flag.

exercises.title: Traverse a locked directory
exercises.description: Restore owner traversal on vault, then read vault/receipt.

exercises.title: Recover after a failed check
exercises.description: Use test and || to create restored.txt containing recovered when missing.txt does not exist.

exercises.title: Count accepted records
exercises.description: Count lines containing ACCEPT in traffic.txt and write the count to count.txt.

chapters.title: Advanced: automation checkpoints
chapters.description: Put it all together. These checkpoints chain several skills into one task, the way real investigations and automation work.
chapters.summary: Put it all together. These checkpoints chain several skills into one task, the way real investigations and automation work.

exercises.title: Normalize a status stream
exercises.description: Translate status.txt to lowercase and save it as normalized.txt.

exercises.title: Order numeric priorities
exercises.description: Sort priorities.txt numerically and save the smallest value to first.txt.

exercises.title: Clean the staging folder
exercises.description: Remove the two temporary files in staging, then remove the empty staging directory. Preserve keep.txt.

exercises.title: Advanced checkpoint: restore the relay
exercises.description: Locate dispatch.dat under /opt/academy, select the RELEASE record, decode its second colon-delimited field, and save the decoded flag in /home/user/final.txt. Submit that flag.

chapters.title: Operator: running programs
chapters.description: Flags now belong to root. Learn how Linux finds and starts programs, so you can make them hand the flag over.
chapters.summary: The flag now belongs to root, so you cannot simply read it. Mission programs run with root privileges and hand it over only when you start them correctly, which means understanding how Linux finds and runs programs.
skills: Read ownership in ls -l and see why /flag is off limits
Run programs in the current directory with ./ (and know why the dot is needed)

exercises.title: A locked flag and an absolute launch
exercises.description: Run the beacon program in /opt/relay/bin by its absolute path to get the flag.

exercises.title: Run it from right here
exercises.description: Go to /opt/relay/bin and start the uplink program there with a relative path that begins with ./

exercises.title: Launch from the right place
exercises.description: Run /opt/relay/bin/ignite. It names the directory it must be launched from. Go there with cd and run it again by its absolute path.

exercises.title: Checkpoint: find the live launcher
exercises.description: One launcher in /opt/relay/bin is live and hidden. List everything in that directory, dotfiles included, and run the live launcher by its full path. Ignore the retired one.

chapters.title: Operator: arguments and documentation
chapters.description: Make programs do what you want: options with values, --help, manual pages and exit statuses.
chapters.summary: Programs do what their arguments tell them. Learn to find the right options from a README, from --help and from a manual page, and to read the exit status every command leaves behind.
skills: Pass options that take their own values
Search long manual pages with man | grep

exercises.title: An option with a value
exercises.description: Read /opt/vault/README, then use the vault command to read /flag for you.

exercises.title: Ask the program for help
exercises.description: Run codegen --help. Find the option that prints the release key, then pass that key to codegen -k.

exercises.title: Search the manual
exercises.description: The signal program has about 150 options. Its manual (man signal) says which one releases the flag. Find that option and run signal with it.

exercises.title: Read the exit status
exercises.description: Run probe. It fails on purpose with an exit status. Read the status with echo $? straight away, then run report with that number.

chapters.title: Operator: streams and redirection
chapters.description: Standard output, standard error and the file descriptors behind them. Capture, split, append and filter.
chapters.summary: Every program has a standard output and a standard error. Capture them, split them, append instead of overwrite, and filter output that would otherwise flood your screen.
skills: Redirect standard output to a file
Merge streams with 2>&1 before a pipe

exercises.title: Capture standard output
exercises.description: Run transmit with its standard output redirected to capture.log, then read capture.log.

exercises.title: Split the streams
exercises.description: Run relay so its standard output goes to data.log and its standard error goes to notes.log. Then read both files: the flag is in one of them.

exercises.title: Append, don't overwrite
exercises.description: assemble writes the first half of the flag straight into /home/user/assembled.txt, then prints the second half. Redirect its output into that same file so the two halves join up.

exercises.title: Filter the error stream
exercises.description: flood prints 1,500 status lines on standard error and one of them holds the flag. Get its standard error into grep and pull out the line containing CYBER.

chapters.title: Operator: pipelines and variables
chapters.description: Multi-stage pipelines, intercepting them with tee, exported versus local variables, read, and the final Operator checkpoint.
chapters.summary: Build multi-stage pipelines, debug them with tee, control which variables programs can see, and finish with the Operator checkpoint.
skills: Chain three programs with two pipes
Tell local variables from exported ones
Read values into variables with read NAME < FILE

exercises.title: Two pipes, three programs
exercises.description: codes prints 20 launch codes, but only into a pipe, never to your screen. verify wants exactly the first 7. Connect codes to verify with head in between.

exercises.title: Intercept a pipe with tee
exercises.description: emitter | receiver fails, and emitter only explains why into the pipe. Put tee between them to save what emitter sends, read that copy, then run the pipeline again correctly.

exercises.title: Local or exported?
exercises.description: Run clearance with OPERATOR set to relay and exported, and CALLSIGN set to night but not exported.

exercises.title: Read straight into a variable
exercises.description: /opt/relay/rotating.key changes after every command you run. Load the current key into the KEY variable in a single command.

exercises.title: Operator checkpoint: the hidden uplink
exercises.description: A hidden uplink program sits somewhere under /var/spool. Run it from /tmp on the ACTIVE channel listed in /opt/relay/channels.txt. It only talks into a pipe, and its payload comes out reversed.
